mcq.q: Which category is NOT one of the standard peripheral categories given in the notes?
mcq.explanation: The notes list input, output, storage and communication devices. Processing units are part of the CPU.

mcq.q: A modem or network card belongs to which peripheral category?
mcq.explanation: Communication devices connect the computer to other systems.

mcq.q: Which function of the I/O interface converts data between serial and parallel form?
mcq.explanation: Interfaces convert serial data to parallel and back, and digital to analog and back.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT an interface command?
mcq.explanation: The four commands are control, status, data input and data output.

mcq.q: In handshaking, RTS stands for:
mcq.explanation: RTS = Request to Send, sent by the transmitter to say it is ready to send.

mcq.q: In handshaking, CTS stands for:
mcq.explanation: CTS = Clear to Send, the receiver's reply that it is ready to accept data.

mcq.q: A strobe signal sent BEFORE the data is called:
mcq.explanation: Leading strobe comes before the data; trailing strobe comes after.

mcq.q: Which device generates the strobe signal in a source-initiated strobe?
mcq.explanation: In source-initiated strobe, the sender generates the strobe.

mcq.q: In asynchronous transmission, each character is framed by:
mcq.explanation: Start and stop bits mark the beginning and end of each character.

mcq.q: Which transmission sends data in frames or blocks?
mcq.explanation: Synchronous transmission sends frames or blocks at fixed intervals.

mcq.q: During DMA the CPU:
options: Is idle and has no control over the memory buses
mcq.explanation: The DMA controller takes over the buses; the CPU is idle during the transfer.

mcq.q: Which mode is best for fast devices and bulk transfers without CPU involvement?
mcq.explanation: DMA moves data directly between device and memory.

mcq.q: In interrupt initiated I/O, after servicing the interrupt the CPU:
mcq.explanation: CPU services the transfer and resumes the earlier task.

mcq.q: The main disadvantage of programmed I/O is:
options: It keeps the CPU busy during transfers
mcq.explanation: CPU must monitor and transfer each item, degrading system performance.

mcq.q: Which memory is the first to be accessed by the CPU in the memory hierarchy?
mcq.explanation: Cache is checked first, since it is the fastest and closest to the CPU.

mcq.q: The ROM part of main memory stores:
mcq.explanation: Bootstrap loader starts the computer when power is turned on.

mcq.q: Which RAM needs refreshing circuitry?
mcq.explanation: Dynamic RAM stores bits in capacitors, which leak charge and must be refreshed.

mcq.q: Compared to SRAM, DRAM has:
options: More memory cells per unit area
Fewer memory cells per unit area
mcq.explanation: DRAM has more cells per area, which is why it is used for main memory.

mcq.q: Processes are loaded into primary memory because:
options: Secondary memory cannot be accessed directly by the CPU
mcq.explanation: CPU can access only primary memory directly, so ready processes are loaded there.

mcq.q: In magnetic tape, data is recorded as:
options: Bits in parallel across all tracks
Seven or nine bits per character with a parity bit
mcq.explanation: Seven or nine bits are recorded together with a parity bit to form a character.

mcq.q: Hard disk is also called:
mcq.explanation: Hard disks are permanently attached to the unit, so they are called fixed disks.

mcq.q: Cache memory is commonly how many times faster than RAM (per the notes)?
mcq.explanation: Notes say cache is 10 to 100 times faster than RAM.

mcq.q: Which is correct about access time in the hierarchy?
options: Primary memory access time is less than secondary and greater than cache
Secondary memory is faster than cache
mcq.explanation: Cache is fastest, then primary (RAM), then secondary memory.

mcq.q: Static RAM is used in:
mcq.explanation: Static RAM is fast and used to implement cache.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT given as an asynchronous transfer example on the slide?
mcq.explanation: Slide examples are email, forum and radio.

mcq.q: A strobe signal sent AFTER the data is called:
mcq.explanation: Trailing strobe comes after the data; leading strobe comes before.

mcq.q: In asynchronous transmission, data is sent in the form of:
mcq.explanation: Slide: asynchronous data is sent as bytes or characters; synchronous data is sent in frames or blocks.

mcq.q: A buffer in data transfer is:
options: A short-term location for storing incoming or departing data
mcq.explanation: Slide definition of buffer.

mcq.q: Compared with asynchronous transmission, synchronous transmission is:
options: Based on start and stop bits
mcq.explanation: Slide: synchronous is faster (and costlier); asynchronous is slower and cheaper.

mcq.q: In Programmed I/O, the I/O device cannot:
mcq.explanation: Slide: I/O device cannot direct-access memory, so the CPU program must control each transfer.

mcq.q: In Programmed I/O, the flag bit F is kept in the:
mcq.explanation: The interface sets the flag F in its status register.

mcq.q: Which characteristic belongs to interrupt-initiated I/O?
options: Reduces CPU involvement during idle times
Inefficient for devices with unpredictable response
mcq.explanation: Slide: interrupt mode is asynchronous, reduces CPU involvement during idle times, and suits unpredictable or slow devices.

mcq.q: The modes of data transfer aim to manage the trade-off between:
options: CPU involvement and data transfer speed
mcq.explanation: Slide: different modes manage CPU involvement against transfer speed.

mcq.q: In DMA, which signal does the DMA controller send to request the bus from the processor?
mcq.explanation: BR goes to the processor's HOLD input; the processor acknowledges with HLDA and sends BG.

mcq.q: During DMA, the CPU:
options: Is idle and has no control over the memory buses
mcq.explanation: Slide: during DMA the CPU is idle and the DMA controller takes over the buses.

mcq.q: The slide describes secondary memory as:
options: External and not directly accessible by the CPU
mcq.explanation: Secondary memory is external, non-volatile and not directly accessible by the processor.

mcq.q: Which statement about Dynamic RAM is correct?
options: It stores charge on a capacitor and needs refreshing
mcq.explanation: DRAM uses capacitor charge and refresh circuitry.

mcq.q: RAM is also known as:
mcq.explanation: Slide: RAM is known as computer memory or main memory.

mcq.q: The bootstrap loader is stored in:
mcq.explanation: The ROM portion of main memory holds the bootstrap loader, which starts the computer when power is on.

mcq.q: Which ROM type can be programmed by the user only once?
mcq.explanation: PROM: the user writes a blank PROM once; it cannot be altered afterwards.

mcq.q: Which statement about the memory hierarchy is correct?
options: Access speed is the same for all memory types
Cache and main memory are faster but smaller and costlier
mcq.explanation: Slide: cache and main memory are faster but smaller and more costly; access speed varies by type.

mcq.q: Which of these is a primary memory type on the slide classification?
mcq.explanation: Primary memory = RAM (SRAM, DRAM) and ROM (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM).

mcq.q: Magnetic tape records a character as:
options: Seven or nine bits plus a parity bit
mcq.explanation: Slide: usually 7 or 9 bits form a character together with a parity bit.

mcq.q: Which secondary storage is permanently attached to the unit and cannot be removed by an occasional user?
mcq.explanation: Slide: disks permanently attached to the unit assembly are called hard disks.

mcq.q: Which of these is an optical disk storage device?
mcq.explanation: CD is an optical disk; pen drive is flash memory; hard disk and tape are magnetic.

mcq.q: Which device is classified as flash memory on the slide?
mcq.explanation: Slide classification: flash memory -> pen drive.

mcq.q: Cache memory is described as:
mcq.explanation: Slide: cache is a fast and small memory.

mcq.q: The primary role of cache memory is to:
options: Reduce the average time taken to access data
mcq.explanation: Slide: cache reduces average access time and improves performance.

mcq.q: According to the slides, cache memory is how many times faster than RAM?
mcq.explanation: Slide: 10 to 100 times faster than RAM.

short.q: Explain the RTS and CTS signals in handshaking.
short.answer: RTS (Request to Send) is sent by the transmitter when it is ready to provide data. CTS (Clear to Send) is the receiver's reply when it is ready to accept the data.

short.q: Differentiate between leading strobe and trailing strobe.
short.answer: A leading strobe is sent before the data; a trailing strobe is sent after the data.

short.q: How does DMA differ from interrupt initiated I/O?
short.answer: In interrupt I/O the CPU still transfers data after the interrupt. In DMA a controller takes over the buses and transfers data directly between device and memory while the CPU is idle.

short.q: Why is DMA preferred for magnetic disks?
short.answer: Disks are fast and transfer large blocks; DMA moves them directly into memory without CPU involvement, so the transfer is efficient.

short.q: What functions does an I/O interface perform? Name any three.
short.answer: Synchronizes CPU and device speeds; selects the right device; provides control and timing signals; data buffering; error detection; serial to parallel and digital to analog conversion (any three).

short.q: What is a bootstrap loader and where is it stored?
short.answer: It is a small initial program stored in ROM that starts the computer software when power is turned on.

short.q: Why is DRAM preferred for main memory even though it needs refreshing?
short.answer: It stores more cells per unit area, so it gives more capacity at lower cost, while SRAM is used for faster cache.

short.q: What is the access style of magnetic tape and what is it mainly used for?
short.answer: Sequential access, meaning data must be read in order. It is mainly used for backup.

A separate strobe signal, generated by the transmitting device, is sent with the data to show when the data on the bus is valid. It is sent before the data (leading strobe) or after it (trailing strobe).

short.q: What is handshaking and why is it used in asynchronous transfer?
short.answer: Handshaking is a method in which the two devices exchange control signals (RTS/CTS, or data valid/data accepted) so both are ready before data moves. It guarantees synchronized and dependable data delivery.
The CPU must constantly monitor the device and transfer every data item through program instructions, so the processor stays busy and overall system performance is degraded.

short.q: What are the BR and BG signals in DMA?
short.answer: BR (bus request) is sent by the DMA controller to the processor's HOLD input to request the bus. The processor acknowledges with HLDA and then sends BG (bus grant) to the DMA controller.

short.q: Why are programs and data kept in secondary memory, while the CPU runs them from primary memory?
short.answer: Secondary memory is larger and cheaper, so it stores all programs and data. The CPU cannot access secondary memory directly, so the OS loads the required process into primary memory, which the CPU can access quickly.

short.q: Explain the difference between a track and a sector on a magnetic disk.
short.answer: A track is one of the concentric circles on the disk surface. A track is divided into sectors, and a sector is the minimum quantity of information transferred.

short.q: Why is magnetic tape slower to access than a disk?
short.answer: Magnetic tape is sequential access storage, so the tape must be read in order to reach the required data, which increases access time.

short.q: Why is cache memory placed between the CPU and main memory?
short.answer: It acts as a buffer and provides faster access to active data. This reduces the average time taken to access data and improves overall system performance.
